C-HISTORICAL-ASSERTION-REVIEW-2-67E62A9B.IntentSummary:
T3 plan for C-HISTORICAL-ASSERTION-REVIEW-2-67E62A9B, the lineage-2 successor authored from the maintainer-ratified spec (SHA-256 `b2be363a1ed744b6bf60a61ee61fcd5b90c3d29b3f0e7956e93432314075d22a`, `status` `approved`, permit recorded in the bundle's `run-ledger.xml` at `baseCommit` `e1fb45886da1f8d88985a26d87d8dc7dfdd70b4a`). It preserves the archived predecessor's `plan.xml` (`C-HISTORICAL-ASSERTION-REVIEW-1-C6AA9BFE`) as lineage input, not as approved executable authority: status resets to `draft`, the verb-inserted `Replacement` child is dropped, artifact identity and lifecycle paths are re-homed to the successor, and `src/grace-lint.test.ts` is added to the forced test set and every write-population allowlist. Every normative byte-invariance and write-population guard keeps the spec's committed base `e1fb45886da1f8d88985a26d87d8dc7dfdd70b4a`; only the lifecycle checkpoint (this plan's authoring HEAD) is newer.
**Boundary.** Current workdir XML defines current validation; history is metadata, never mandatory retrospective current compliance. Current obligations (root context, graph, verification, active change bundles, and the selected current close) stay strict; unrelated archived change bundles leave current lint entirely (no error, no warning); historical reads (`change show`, `context --change` on an archive, a bare `review --change`) report supported fields and distinguish `unavailable` from `absent`; historical integrity audits (F286 attempt-pair, F16 relocation/foreign-ID detection) remain informational and non-blocking.
**Owning modules and their verification siblings.** `M-GRAMMAR` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts` and `src/artifact/scope.ts`), `M-QUERY` (`src/query/core.ts`, `src/query/change.ts`, `src/query/render.ts`), `M-LINT-CORE` (`src/lint/core.ts`), `M-REVIEW` (`src/review/core.ts`, `src/review/catalog.ts`), and `M-GATES` (`src/gates/ledger.ts`), paired with `V-M-GRAMMAR`, `V-M-QUERY`, `V-M-LINT-CORE`, `V-M-REVIEW`, and `V-M-GATES`. Every owning module appears in the spec's `AffectedAreas` and in this plan's `DurableScope`; each production path carries a `LINKS:` to its module. `.test.ts` paths are not module-ownable write paths, so no synthetic `LINKS:` header or new graph anchor is added for them. `src/grace-context.ts` is deliberately not in scope: the spec records its existing refusal and `unable-to-determine` shapes as the bound historical-context contract, and the unrelated-malformed-archive fix lives in grammar/query.
**Ordering and dependencies.** T-001 removes archived change bundles from current validation (grammar/query/lint) and binds the `src/grace-lint.test.ts` wrapper regression, and is the foundation every later task builds on. T-002 makes applied scope credit field-level and is the substrate for the historical view's `unavailable` classification. T-003 adds the `ChangeView` unavailable union and its text/JSON consumers. T-004 turns the archived `MustExist` audit into the `review.historical-path-absent` information notice and registers it. T-005 repairs the T-005 guard and the CLI exit pair, in the same test file T-004 edits, so it depends on T-004. T-006 is the selected-close evidence contract and depends only on T-001; T-007 is the historical-context overturn regression and depends only on T-001; both are independent of the review work. T-008 corrects the `ngrace-plan` rule-19 meaning and its footprint pins and depends on T-005 and T-006 because the corrected text states the audit and close behavior those tasks establish. The executor runs the plan serially with no concurrent workers, branches, or worktrees; the dependency edges, not file adjacency, set the order.
**All 19 approved `AC-*` are close-bound with 21 `CloseEvidence` commands**, so no task carries `<Satisfies>`; a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion is an error, and this plan adds none.
**Assertions.** `BaselineAssertions` bind only facts the deliverable leaves unchanged: the five module anchors, their `MustVerify` siblings, and stable symbols in the touched files. The deliverable intentionally flips `validateNgraceProject`'s archive walk, the archived-`MustExist` finding code, the rule-19 scratch clause, and the `ChangeView` shape, so none of those pre-edit forms is pinned as a baseline. `TargetAssertions` bind the post-edit facts and carry exactly one `MustPassCommand`, `bun run validate:ci`, driven statically with `--assertions target` (which reports the command unevaluated by design) and then with `--assertions final --run-commands`.
**Close execution order (guidance; the authority owns the real gates).** The close is a two-verdict sequence: pre-archive `ngrace review` supplies findings for `gate verdict`, which permits `gate apply`; `gate apply` and `gate archive` then permit; `ngrace apply` writes applied statuses and moves the bundle into the archive; a post-archive `ngrace gate verdict --change C-ID --outcome pass` evaluates every `CloseEvidence` command in the applied-archive state and records a `Result`/`Exit` pair per criterion through the shipped `ngrace change show`. The post-archive verdict refuses `pass` on any failed or incomplete `CloseEvidence`; the pre-archive verdict does not evaluate `CloseEvidence`. The archive gate requires an empty `run/`, so a terminal cursor event precedes `cursor fold`. Exactly two whole-CI evidence locations exist: the `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` under `--assertions final --run-commands`, and the post-archive `AC-CI-GREEN` `CloseEvidence`. No invocation count is claimed. No record payment/flush is authorized; no stash action is authorized.
**`ObservedWriteScope`.** The 23 approved implementation/support/test paths, the active lifecycle artifacts (`run.xml`, `run-ledger.xml`, and the `run/**` loose-event glob), and this bundle's own archive arrival glob. The bundle's own `spec.xml`, `plan.xml`, and `design-context.xml` are not listed because review skips them by identity; the whole active and archive bundle directories are already excluded by the spec's `AC-WRITE-POPULATION`.

T-001.Title: Remove archived change bundles from current validation and bind the wrapper regression

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `src/artifact/grammar.ts` no longer emits current-format validation issues for archived change bundles: `validateChangeBundlesInDirectory` skips the archive location (or otherwise excludes it from the returned issues), so an archived spec or plan that is malformed, that declares a non-current `graceVersion`, or that parses with the installed version but omits a current-only required section such as `Summary` contributes no error and no warning. Active change bundles, root context, graph, and verification artifacts are validated unchanged.

`src/query/core.ts` `collectOperationalValidationErrors` extracts assertions and scopes from active plans only, so an unrelated archived assertion defect cannot make `loadGraceArtifactIndex` throw; `ngrace status` and `ngrace context` load with such an archive present.

`src/lint/core.ts` `validateAssertions` no longer extracts or evaluates archived plans in the current lint result; a malformed archived plan produces no `xml.parse` and no `change.applied-plan-missing` lint issue, and a malformed **active** plan still refuses.

`src/grace-lint.test.ts` corrects the archived malformed-plan expectation at `src/grace-lint.test.ts:2303` from `change.applied-plan-missing === true` to `false` while the active `asStatus="applied"` preview at `:2318` keeps `change.applied-plan-missing === true` and the well-formed active control at `:2331` keeps it `false`. This is the direct regression for `AC-WRAPPER-REGRESSION` and uses the spec's exact selector `-t "emits change.applied-plan-missing at applied when plan.xml carries no previewable status"`.

`src/artifact/grammar.test.ts` gains a test selectable by `-t "archived history is not a current obligation"` driving each of the three archived cases (version change, same-version missing `Summary`, malformed) through every bound surface on a physical throwaway copy: `bun run ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings` exits 0 with empty error and warning counts, `loadGraceArtifactIndex` loads, and `ngrace status` and `ngrace context` succeed; after each mutation the exact original bytes are restored and the exact base output returns (not only exit 0). A test selectable by `-t "active stays strict"` proves a malformed active artifact still refuses. `src/grace-query.test.ts` and `src/lint/core.test.ts` gain the index-tolerance and archived-assertion-lint regressions.

Verification.Command: bun test --timeout=0 src/artifact/grammar.test.ts -t "archived history is not a current obligation"
bun test --timeout=0 src/artifact/grammar.test.ts -t "active stays strict"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-query.test.ts -t "unrelated archive does not block the index"
bun test --timeout=0 src/lint/core.test.ts -t "archived assertions leave current lint"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-lint.test.ts -t "emits change.applied-plan-missing at applied when plan.xml carries no previewable status"

T-002.Title: Grant applied-scope credit only from readable scope fields

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `src/artifact/scope.ts` `collectAppliedChangeScopes`/`readAppliedChangeScope` grants durable and observed scope credit only when the applied archived plan parses and its durable/observed scope fields are readable; an unparsable plan, or a scope field carrying an uninterpretable shape (`scope.invalid-durable-shape` / `scope.invalid-observed-shape` / `scope.invalid-context-artifact`, and also `scope.none-with-entries`, `scope.invalid-path`, and `scope.unsupported-glob`), yields no credit for that field and is distinguishable from a legitimate `declared-none`/empty scope; a genuine section absence is distinct from an explicit `<None />`; a readable sibling field remains usable. A present but structurally empty field supplies zero credit and is not promoted to empty credit. The observed field's credit is proven at its actual consumer, the `collectProjectStatus` observed-drift decision (`grace-status.ts` uses `scope.observedWrites` for explained-file credit). There is no applied-durable drift consumer, so durable readability is proven through the applied-scope reader that `change show` presents, and a readable archived bundle's applied observed scope still explains drift exactly as today.

`src/artifact/scope.test.ts` gains a test selectable by `-t "unreadable history grants no credit"` driving the applied-scope reader over both directions (invalid/empty durable with valid observed, invalid/empty observed with valid durable), the `None`-mixed-with-entries, invalid-path, unsupported-glob, invalid-context-artifact, unparsable-plan, present-empty, genuine-absence, readable-control, and explicit-`None` cases; at the same selector it also drives the observed-drift consumer holding the changed file constant across a readable→`None`+entry→readable mutation, so lost and restored observed credit are both observed on that one file, and asserts durable readability through the applied-scope reader.

Verification.Command: bun test --timeout=0 src/artifact/scope.test.ts -t "unreadable history grants no credit"
bun test --timeout=0 src/artifact/scope.test.ts -t "observedWriteScopeContains"

T-003.Title: Add the ChangeView unavailable union and its text and JSON consumers

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `src/query/change.ts` types `ChangeDurableScope = carried | declared-none | absent | { state: "unavailable"; reason: string }` and `ChangeView.observedWriteScope = ChangeScopeSummary | { state: "unavailable"; reason: string } | null`, with a **nonempty** reason and **no** scope payload on the unavailable member. Selection rules: a supported historical shape yields `carried`/summary regardless of `graceVersion`; a present but structurally empty durable section yields `carried` with the six empty arrays and an empty observed section yields `{ files: [], globs: [] }`; a genuine section absence yields `absent`/`null`; an explicit `<None />` yields the existing shape (durable `declared-none`, observed empty summary); an uninterpretable shape (`scope.invalid-durable-shape`, `scope.invalid-observed-shape`, `scope.invalid-context-artifact`, `scope.none-with-entries`, `scope.invalid-path`, `scope.unsupported-glob`) yields `unavailable` with the reason.

`src/query/render.ts` `formatChangeText`/`formatDurableScope` narrow the union and report the unavailable state and reason distinctly from absent/declared-none; JSON emission (`src/grace-change.ts:118`) carries the exact union member.

`src/query/change.test.ts` is narrowed under the union and gains a test selectable by `-t "historical view unavailable contract"` driving the controls — applied archived known-field fixture, explicit `None`, genuine section absence, present-empty section, an unknown observed child, an observed `None` plus entry, and an uninterpretable shape — through both real `ngrace change show` JSON and text; the text format asserts the unavailable **reason**, not only the word `unavailable`, and the no-plan control and the active controls are retained separately.

Verification.Command: bun test --timeout=0 src/query/change.test.ts -t "historical view unavailable contract"
bunx tsc --noEmit

T-004.Title: Make the archived MustExist audit informational and register the historical-path notice

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `src/review/core.ts` `detectConfidentlyWrong` emits `review.historical-path-absent` at `info` for an archived plan's missing `MustExist` (runtime path or change-bundle artifact path), never `review.confidently-wrong`; the same-ID archive alias present is silent, and the missing-both-alias and foreign-id cases are reported as historical notices whose message or explanation contains `archive-time` and `unevaluated`. Active plans keep `review.confidently-wrong` / `must-exist-missing` with the corr-171 same-ID alias resolution, missing-both refusal, and foreign-ID refusal.

`src/review/catalog.ts` registers `review.historical-path-absent` with `severity: "info"` and `family: "process-audit"`; `patternReviewCodes()` still returns exactly the five family-A codes; the info set is exactly `{review.attempt-pair-unpaired-pass, review.historical-path-absent}`; `allReviewCodes()` is 21 and `excludedReviewCodesForLocalization()` is 18. `src/verification/localize.test.ts` count pins are repaired consistently.

`src/review/core.test.ts` gains tests selectable by `-t "current obligations stay strict"`, `-t "archived existence claim is a historical audit"`, `-t "historical integrity audits preserved"`, and `-t "historical-path notice catalog contract"`. The preserved-audits test exercises the promised behavior, not catalog membership alone: the F286 attempt-pair audit reddens an `applied` archived bundle at `warning` and exempts `superseded`/`rejected`/`cancelled`; the unemitted verification `Marker` check fires; the scope, `WriteEvidence`-scope, verdict, approval, and close-evidence audit codes, severities, and finding IDs still hold; and retirement still consumes archive directory names. Its existing `allReviewCodes()` length pins and info-set pin are updated to 21 and the two-code set.

bun test --timeout=0 src/review/core.test.ts -t "archived existence claim is a historical audit"
bun test --timeout=0 src/review/core.test.ts -t "historical integrity audits preserved"

T-006.Title: Close every selected-close empty-evaluation variant in the gate verdict seam

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `src/gates/ledger.ts` `evaluateCloseEvidenceChildren` / `recordReviewVerdict` refuse `gate verdict --outcome pass` for a bundle resolved under `archive/` unless the spec is readable, uses the `NgraceChangeSpec` root, carries exactly one direct `C-*` wrapper whose tag equals the bundle id, declares `status="applied"`, and has a present, interpretable `AcceptanceCriteria` container with at least one valid anchored `AC-*` criterion **or** a valid legacy `Criterion` child or nonempty legacy criteria text. A complete `CloseEvidence` command executes and a non-zero command refuses `pass` with the existing refusal; an incomplete `CloseEvidence` child (no `Command` or an empty `Command`) refuses `pass` rather than being silently uncounted, and every attached evidence child is validated before criterion filtering can hide it; a missing/malformed container, wrong or missing wrapper identity, unparsable spec, and unavailable applied status all refuse and never fall through to the pre-archive empty-return path. A criterion that carries multiple CloseEvidence siblings records exactly one result child (one row per criterion, never one per evidence block), with `Result` failing if any sibling command fails so a later success never overwrites a failure. A readable applied wrapper with a valid container and genuinely no `CloseEvidence` child at all — anchored or legacy — still permits `pass`, and the active pre-archive empty path is preserved.

`src/gates/core.test.ts` gains a test selectable by `-t "selected close refuses empty evidence evaluation"` driving the public `gate verdict` across every listed variant, including separate anchored, legacy `Criterion`, and legacy direct-text zero-command controls and exact restoration to the base behavior; and a test selectable by `-t "records one result per criterion across multiple evidence siblings"` driving the public `gate verdict`, then reading both `change show` JSON and text, for one criterion with two passing CloseEvidence siblings (exactly one result row) and for the passing-then-failing and failing-then-passing controls (refusal).

Verification.Command: bun test --timeout=0 src/gates/core.test.ts -t "selected close refuses empty evidence evaluation"
bun test --timeout=0 src/gates/core.test.ts -t "records one result per criterion across multiple evidence siblings"
bun test --timeout=0 src/gates/core.test.ts -t "permits unable-to-determine"
